title: Rate and Reasons for Rejection by Applicants Invited to Select Flats in BTO or Sale of Balance Flats Exercise
what_it_is: Rate and Reasons for Rejection by Applicants Invited to Select Flats in BTO or Sale of Balance Flats Exercise

sections.label: Flat applicant reasons and selection
sections.summary: HDB shortlists applicants up to 300% of flat supply, selection takes about six months for BTO and 10 months for SBF, and unbooked flats go to future SBF exercises.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The top three reasons given by these invited flat applicants were that their preferred units had been taken up, they would like to apply for flats in other sales exercises, or they had changed their minds and would like to consider other housing options.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: HDB shortlists flat applicants up to 300% of the flat supply.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Depending on the flat supply and application rate, the average time taken to complete the selection of a BTO exercise and a SBF exercise is around six months and 10 months respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Flats which are not booked will be consolidated for offer in future SBF exercises.

sections.label: HDB queue arrangement rationale
sections.summary: HDB found this a better arrangement than keeping unsuccessful applicants in the queue, who might wait longer without certainty flats would be available.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: HDB has found this to be a better arrangement than having unsuccessful applicants stay in the queue, as the applicants may then end up having to wait for an even longer period of time, without any certainty that the flats will be available.
